nodes.title: Cisco ISE (CCNP Security): Key Ideas
nodes.content: Cisco Identity Services Engine (ISE) is the centralized policy engine for network access control. CCNP Security tests the 802.1X authentication flow, MAB as a fallback for non-supplicant devices, TrustSec for group-based segmentation, posture assessment to check device health before granting access, and profiling to identify device types.

flashcards.front: 802.1X: authenticator, supplicant, authentication server — define each.
flashcards.back: Supplicant: the end device (a laptop running a 802.1X client like Cisco AnyConnect or Windows native supplicant) that presents credentials. Authenticator: the network device (switch port or WLC) that enforces the policy — it starts out blocking all traffic except EAP. Authentication server: typically ISE running RADIUS — validates credentials against AD/LDAP and returns a RADIUS Accept with a VLAN/dACL authorization result.

flashcards.front: MAB — when and why is it used?
flashcards.back: MAC Authentication Bypass is the fallback for devices that don't support 802.1X (printers, IP phones, IoT sensors). The switch sends the device's MAC address as both username and password to the RADIUS server. ISE looks up the MAC in its endpoint database and assigns a policy. MAB is weaker than 802.1X (MAC addresses are spoofable) — assign MAB devices to a restricted VLAN with limited access rights.

flashcards.front: TrustSec SGT — what is it and how does it enable segmentation?
flashcards.back: Security Group Tags are 16-bit labels assigned to traffic when it enters the TrustSec domain (at the authenticating switch). SGTs propagate with the traffic (inline tagging or via SGT Exchange Protocol). Enforcement nodes use Security Group ACLs (SGACLs) to permit or deny based on source SGT + destination SGT pairs — e.g., 'employees (SGT 10) may not reach PCI servers (SGT 50)'. This gives policy-based micro-segmentation without static VLANs.

flashcards.front: Posture assessment — what does ISE check and what happens on failure?
flashcards.back: Posture assessment verifies that a device meets a health policy before granting full access: OS patch level, AV installed and up-to-date, firewall enabled, disk encryption on. The ISE posture agent (part of AnyConnect) runs these checks. Compliant → full access VLAN. Non-compliant → quarantine VLAN with internet access only (to download patches) or complete block. Periodic reassessment can revoke access if the device falls out of compliance during the session.

nodes.title: Cryptography fundamentals: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Crypto is the math layer that makes the rest of security possible. Most exam questions test symmetric vs asymmetric, hashing vs encryption, when to use which, and how key management actually works in practice.

flashcards.front: Symmetric vs asymmetric encryption — when do you use each?
flashcards.back: Symmetric (AES-256, ChaCha20): one shared key, fast, used for bulk data. Asymmetric (RSA, ECC): public/private key pair, slow, used to exchange a symmetric key or to sign. Real systems use both: asymmetric to negotiate, symmetric to encrypt the bulk traffic (this is how TLS works).

flashcards.front: What's the difference between hashing and encryption?
flashcards.back: Encryption is reversible — the holder of the key can recover the plaintext. Hashing is one-way — you cannot derive the input from the output. Hashes are for integrity (did the file change?) and password storage (compare hashes, never store plaintext). SHA-256 is the modern default; MD5 and SHA-1 are broken.

flashcards.front: What is a digital signature?
flashcards.back: A signature is a hash of the message encrypted with the signer's private key. Anyone with the public key can verify (decrypt the signature, recompute the hash, check they match). This proves authenticity (the holder of the private key signed it) AND integrity (the message wasn't tampered with).

flashcards.front: Why use a key management service (KMS)?
flashcards.back: Raw key handling is hard to do safely — you have to rotate, audit, restrict, destroy. A KMS holds keys in hardware, exposes encrypt/decrypt APIs, logs every use, enforces who can use which key. Your application code never sees the actual key material. AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS all play this role.

questions.q: An engineer is hardening the control plane of a core Cisco IOS-XE router. Traffic destined to the router itself (routing protocol updates, SSH, SNMP) must be rate-limited and classified so that a flood of ICMP does not exhaust CPU. Which feature should be configured?
choices: Unicast Reverse Path Forwarding (uRPF) in strict mode
Hardware-based ACL on each ingress interface denying ICMP
Control Plane Policing (CoPP) with a service-policy applied to
Storm Control on uplink interfaces with ICMP threshold
questions.explanation: CoPP classifies traffic punted to the route processor into policy classes (routing, management, monitoring, undesirable) and applies rate-limiters so that floods of any single class cannot starve legitimate control-plane traffic. uRPF addresses source spoofing, ACLs do not rate-limit, and Storm Control is a Layer 2 feature on data-plane interfaces.

questions.q: A security architect wants to prevent rogue DHCP servers on an access switch and also stop ARP spoofing between hosts in the same VLAN. Which combination of features must be enabled?
choices: DHCP snooping with trusted uplinks.
Port-security sticky with DHCP option 82 insertion
IP Source Guard on access ports with static ARP entries for gateways
BPDU Guard on all access ports and Root Guard on uplinks
questions.explanation: DHCP snooping builds a binding table of legitimate IP-to-MAC-to-port mappings and blocks DHCP server responses on untrusted ports. DAI then validates ARP packets against that binding table, dropping gratuitous ARP spoofs. IP Source Guard complements this by filtering data traffic, but DAI is the specific ARP inspection feature. plus Dynamic ARP Inspection (DAI) referencing the snooping binding table

questions.q: A penetration tester gains access to a VLAN through a vulnerable kiosk and sends double-tagged 802.1Q frames hoping to reach a protected VLAN. Which mitigation specifically prevents this VLAN hopping attack?
choices: Assign native VLAN to the same VLAN as a data VLAN on trunks
Disable DTP and set access ports to switchport
Enable BPDU Guard on all access ports
Enable Root Guard on uplinks
questions.explanation: Double-tagging attacks work when the native VLAN on a trunk is used by normal access ports and when DTP allows unsolicited trunk negotiation. Hardcoding access ports, disabling DTP, using a dedicated unused native VLAN, and tagging it with vlan dot1q tag native prevent the attack. plus assign a dedicated unused native VLAN on trunks and tag native VLANs

questions.q: An engineer configures OSPF authentication between two Cisco routers. The security team requires strong integrity and replay protection rather than plain MD5. Which option should be configured?
choices: neighbor a.b.c.d password cisco
ip ospf authentication null
Authentication using a key chain with
ip ospf message-digest-key 1 md5 cisco
questions.explanation: Modern IOS/IOS-XE supports HMAC-SHA cryptographic authentication for OSPF using key chains with rotation and lifetimes. Legacy MD5 is still available but weaker. BGP-style neighbor password and null authentication are unrelated.

questions.q: An organization wants NTP to be authenticated between routers to prevent an attacker from spoofing time and forging log timestamps. Which configuration is correct?
choices: ntp server 10.1.1.1 prefer
ntp master stratum 5
ntp access-group peer 10
Configure ntp authentication
questions.explanation: NTP authentication requires defining a shared key (ntp authentication-key), enabling authentication (ntp authenticate), marking the key as trusted (ntp trusted-key), and binding it on the server statement. Without all four, messages will not be authenticated. ntp authenticate, and ntp trusted-key on both devices, then reference the key on the ntp server command

questions.q: A malicious actor is performing a MAC flooding attack against an access switch, causing the CAM table to overflow so that the switch fails open and floods frames. Which mitigation stops this attack?
choices: Enable DHCP snooping globally
Increase CAM table size
Enable port-security with a maximum
Set spanning-tree portfast on access ports
questions.explanation: Port-security caps the number of distinct source MACs learned on an access port. When exceeded, the port is restricted or shutdown, preventing the CAM overflow that makes a switch flood frames. DHCP snooping addresses a different attack vector.

questions.q: A security engineer wants to prevent IP address spoofing at the edge of the network so that attackers cannot forge source addresses from inside routed segments. Which IOS feature accomplishes this at the interface level?
choices: uRPF (Unicast Reverse Path
Port-security maximum 1
Control Plane Policing
IP directed broadcast disable
questions.explanation: Strict-mode uRPF accepts a packet only if the source address is reachable via the interface it came in on (symmetric path). This blocks spoofed packets at the edge (BCP 38). CoPP protects the control plane; port-security is Layer 2.

nodes.title: VPN and secure connectivity: Key Ideas
nodes.content: A VPN tunnels private traffic over the public internet, encrypting it end-to-end. Site-to-site VPNs connect networks (e.g., on-prem to cloud); client VPNs connect individual devices to a private network. Both rely on IPsec or SSL/TLS.

flashcards.front: Site-to-site VPN vs client VPN — what's the difference?
flashcards.back: Site-to-site VPN connects two networks (typical: on-prem data center ↔ cloud VPC) using gateway devices on each side. Client VPN connects an individual user's laptop to a private network for remote access. Site-to-site uses IPsec, client VPN often uses SSL or WireGuard.

flashcards.front: IPsec — IKE phase 1 vs phase 2.
flashcards.back: Phase 1 (IKE) authenticates the two peers (pre-shared key or certificate) and builds a secure management channel. Phase 2 negotiates the actual data tunnel (encryption algorithm, key lifetime). Most exam questions test that phase 1 must succeed before phase 2.

flashcards.front: When do you pick a dedicated link over a VPN?
flashcards.back: VPN over the public internet is cheap but variable — bandwidth and latency depend on internet weather. Dedicated links (Direct Connect, ExpressRoute, Cloud Interconnect) are private fiber with consistent latency and bandwidth — pick them for production traffic that must be predictable, or compliance scenarios that forbid the public internet.

flashcards.front: What's the BGP tunnel option for?
flashcards.back: VPNs can use static routes or BGP. BGP-based VPNs auto-propagate route changes between sides (add a new subnet on-prem → cloud learns it within seconds). Static VPN requires manual route updates every time the topology changes. Always pick BGP for production.

questions.q: A financial services company is designing an IPsec site-to-site VPN between two data centers. The security team requires Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS) so that a future compromise of the pre-shared key cannot decrypt previously captured traffic. Which IKEv2 configuration element enforces PFS on every rekey?
choices: Lifetime reduction on the IKEv2 SA to 3600 seconds
A stronger encryption algorithm such as AES-256-GCM in the IKEv2 proposal
Enabling dead peer detection (DPD) on both peers
A Diffie-Hellman group specified in the IPsec (Phase 2) proposal
questions.explanation: PFS is achieved by performing a fresh Diffie-Hellman exchange during each IPsec SA rekey. Configuring a DH group in the IPsec proposal (Phase 2) forces that new exchange, so even if long-term keys are later compromised, previously recorded sessions cannot be decrypted. Stronger ciphers, short lifetimes, and DPD do not by themselves guarantee PFS.

questions.q: An engineer troubleshoots an IKEv2 site-to-site VPN stuck in MM_WAIT_MSG2. Both peers have matching proposals, PSKs, and reachable IPs. Which is the most likely cause?
choices: The ISAKMP authentication method is set to rsa-sig on one peer
The crypto ACLs on the two sides have overlapping subnets
Outbound UDP 500 or UDP 4500 is blocked or NAT is rewriting the
Mismatched IKEv2 lifetime values between peers
questions.explanation: MM_WAIT_MSG2 in the phase-1 state machine means the initiator is waiting for the first response from the peer. The overwhelming cause is Layer 3/4: UDP 500 (or 4500 with NAT-T) is dropped by a firewall or NAT without NAT-T. Proposal, PSK, and ACL mismatches appear in later states.

questions.q: An engineer configures Cisco AnyConnect (Secure Client) remote access VPN on an ASA. Which feature steers only corporate subnets through the tunnel while sending Internet-bound traffic directly?
choices: Transparent firewall mode with BVI
Split tunneling using a split-tunnel-policy
Hair-pinning with same-security-traffic permit intra-interface
Full tunnel with U-turn NAT
questions.explanation: Split tunneling with an include ACL (tunnelspecified) pushes only the listed subnets down the VPN, while everything else uses the client's local Internet. Hair-pinning is used for client-to-client traffic through the same ASA interface, not for Internet offload.

questions.q: An architect is choosing between Cisco DMVPN and GETVPN for a large multi-site MPLS backbone where all sites must freely reach each other and encryption must preserve original source/destination addresses for multicast routing. Which technology fits best?
choices: Site-to-site IKEv1 mesh tunnels
GETVPN (Group Encrypted Transport
FlexVPN hub-spoke with IKEv2
DMVPN Phase 2 with NHRP redirects
questions.explanation: GETVPN uses group keys distributed by a Key Server via GDOI. Because it does not tunnel-encapsulate, the original IP header is preserved, which lets MPLS routing and multicast work natively across the encrypted overlay. DMVPN/FlexVPN tunnel the traffic, changing outer headers.

questions.q: An engineer must decide between Cisco AnyConnect SSL VPN and IPsec IKEv2 remote access. Remote users are often behind hotel NAT and restrictive firewalls that only allow HTTP/HTTPS. Which option is most likely to succeed in all locations?
choices: IKEv2 on UDP 500 with no NAT-T
IKEv1 main mode on UDP 500
AnyConnect SSL VPN over TCP
L2TP over IPsec
questions.explanation: SSL VPN over TCP 443 looks like normal HTTPS and traverses almost any NAT or captive portal. DTLS on UDP 443 accelerates once available. IKEv1/IKEv2 over UDP 500/4500 is frequently blocked in guest/hotel networks.

questions.q: An engineer deploys FlexVPN on a hub-spoke topology using IKEv2. Which feature allows spokes to dynamically build spoke-to-spoke tunnels on demand using shortcut switching?
choices: ASA SSL VPN split tunneling
FlexVPN with NHRP shortcut switching
IKEv1 aggressive mode with wildcard PSK
GETVPN group key distribution
questions.explanation: FlexVPN supports NHRP redirect/shortcut similar to DMVPN Phase 3, allowing the hub to redirect spokes to each other. Spokes then establish direct on-demand tunnels without hair-pinning through the hub.

questions.q: A healthcare company stores PHI in an AWS S3 bucket. They must ensure data is encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys and that access is restricted to specific IAM roles. Which AWS configuration meets these requirements?
choices: Enable SSE-S3 server-side encryption and allow public read with a bucket policy
Enable SSE-KMS with a customer-managed KMS key and restrict access with an IAM role +
Rely on TLS 1.2 in transit; S3 encrypts everything by default
Use client-side encryption with a static key stored in the application config
questions.explanation: SSE-KMS with a customer-managed CMK gives the customer control over key policy, rotation, and audit via CloudTrail. Combining it with an IAM role and a bucket policy referencing the role ARN ensures only authorized identities can decrypt. Public access contradicts PHI protection; hard-coded static keys are bad practice.

questions.q: A CIO is evaluating Cisco Secure Workload (Tetration). Which primary security benefit does it provide beyond traditional perimeter firewalls?
choices: Automatic WAN link optimization between data centers
Certificate lifecycle management for web servers
Application dependency mapping and zero-trust
Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) scrubbing at the edge
questions.explanation: Secure Workload collects telemetry from agents on every workload, discovers application dependencies, then generates and enforces microsegmentation policies (allow-list) at the host level. It works identically on bare metal, VMs, containers, AWS, Azure, and GCP. It is not a WAN optimizer or DDoS scrubber.

questions.q: A CASB product (Cisco Cloudlock) flags that several employees uploaded sensitive CRM records to an unsanctioned third-party SaaS. Which cloud security concept does Cloudlock address?
choices: Kubernetes admission control
Shadow IT discovery and
DNS-layer malware filtering
IaaS hardening via security groups
questions.explanation: CASBs inspect SaaS activity via API and inline modes: they discover Shadow IT, classify data (DLP), and apply policy against unsanctioned or risky sharing. Cloudlock integrates with Salesforce, Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, etc. It is not a DNS or K8s tool.

questions.q: A container security engineer wants to ensure that only signed images from an approved registry can be deployed to a Kubernetes cluster. Which mechanism enforces this at admission time?
choices: An Admission Controller (e.g.
Pod Security Admission labels on namespaces (without additional verification)
A Kubernetes NetworkPolicy denying egress to unknown registries
RBAC ClusterRole limiting who can use kubectl apply
questions.explanation: Admission controllers validate objects before they are persisted. OPA Gatekeeper or Kyverno policies can require images to come from an approved registry and pass cosign signature verification. PSA handles pod security standards, not image provenance. OPA Gatekeeper or Kyverno) policy validating image registry and cosign signatures

questions.q: A cloud team must ensure that EC2 instances cannot reach the Internet but can call AWS services privately. Which configuration meets this?
choices: VPC Interface Endpoints (PrivateLink) for required AWS services and no
Route table with default route to a Transit Gateway toward an on-prem proxy
Public subnet with an Elastic IP and stateful NACL
Security group allowing 0.0.0.0/0 outbound and a NAT Gateway
questions.explanation: VPC endpoints (Gateway for S3/DynamoDB, Interface/PrivateLink for most others) route traffic to AWS services over the AWS private backbone without crossing the Internet. Removing the IGW route ensures the subnet is truly private.

nodes.title: Cisco Firepower NGFW: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Cisco Firepower is Cisco's next-generation firewall platform combining traditional stateful inspection with application visibility, intrusion prevention (NGIPS), and advanced malware protection. CCNP Security exams test its architecture and policy model.

flashcards.front: FMC vs FDM — which is required for multi-device management?
flashcards.back: Firepower Management Center (FMC) manages multiple sensors centrally; Firepower Device Manager (FDM) is an on-box GUI for single-device management only.

flashcards.front: Firepower Access Control Policy hierarchy?
flashcards.back: Default action at the bottom; rules evaluated top-to-bottom first match wins. Each rule can allow, block, or redirect to IPS/AMP inspection.

flashcards.front: What does Snort inspect in Firepower?
flashcards.back: Snort is the inline IPS engine; it applies intrusion rules to decoded network traffic and can drop or alert on matching packets.

flashcards.front: AMP for Networks vs AMP for Endpoints?
flashcards.back: AMP for Networks: file reputation and sandboxing at the network perimeter via Firepower. AMP for Endpoints: host-level continuous monitoring and quarantine.

questions.q: An engineer observes that a Cisco Secure Firewall (FTD) managed by FMC is blocking legitimate HTTPS traffic to a business partner site because SSL decryption cannot inspect it. The partner uses certificate pinning. What is the correct action?
choices: Import the partner's private key into FMC to enable decryption
Create a Do Not Decrypt rule matching the partner domain in the SSL policy
Switch the decryption policy from Decrypt-Resign to Decrypt-Known-Key
Disable the SSL policy entirely on the affected access control rule
questions.explanation: Pinned applications reject any certificate not matching the exact pinned copy, so Decrypt-Resign breaks them. The supported approach is to add a Do Not Decrypt rule for the specific destination (URL category, SNI, or application) while keeping decryption enabled globally. Importing a private key is not possible (you do not own the partner's), and disabling the SSL policy is too broad.

questions.q: A developer integrates a third-party application with Cisco FMC using the REST API. The application retrieves access control rules every 30 seconds. After a week, the requests start failing with HTTP 429. What is the most likely cause?
choices: The API token has expired; generate a new authentication token
The client is missing the Content-Type: application/json header
The FMC is rate-limiting the client because polling frequency exceeds
The FMC REST API requires re-authentication every 1000 calls
questions.explanation: HTTP 429 Too Many Requests indicates rate limiting. FMC caps REST API calls (typically 120 messages per minute per client/IP). Reducing polling frequency, using subscription-based mechanisms, or spacing calls fixes the issue. Expired tokens return 401, missing headers return 415.

questions.q: An engineer is configuring a Cisco Secure Firewall access control policy. A rule must inspect traffic for intrusions using a balanced Snort ruleset and also log connections. What rule action must be used?
choices: Trust (with logging)
Monitor
Allow with an
Block with reset
questions.explanation: The Allow action passes traffic through the AC rule while letting attached inspection (intrusion, file, variable set) run on it. Trust bypasses inspection. Monitor is passive and cannot be terminal. Block prevents traffic entirely.

questions.q: A Cisco Firepower Threat Defense (FTD) deployment must block outbound connections to newly registered domains (NRDs) often associated with phishing. Which feature achieves this without maintaining a manual list?
choices: Security Intelligence (SI) feeds from
NAT rule with destination zone any
Flexible NetFlow sampling
Custom File Policy blocking .zip files
questions.explanation: Security Intelligence uses Talos-maintained feeds (malware, phishing, botnets, NRD, DGA) to block, monitor, or allow traffic by IP/URL/DNS reputation before the access control rules fire. It is updated automatically.

questions.q: A security team is rolling out Cisco Umbrella as the primary DNS-layer security control. The CISO requires that users on managed corporate laptops receive granular, user-level policies even when off the corporate network. Which deployment method meets this requirement?
choices: Deploy Umbrella Virtual Appliances (VAs) in each branch to forward DNS
Point internal DNS forwarders to the Umbrella resolvers using Cisco Secure Network conditional forwarding
Configure DHCP to push Umbrella resolvers 208.67.222.222 and 208.67.220.220
Install the Cisco Umbrella Roaming Client or AnyConnect Umbrella module on endpoints
questions.explanation: DHCP-based and VA-based deployments only work while on the corporate network and identify devices at the network level. The Umbrella Roaming Client (standalone or as an AnyConnect module) follows the device everywhere, encrypts DNS to Umbrella, and supports granular user/identity-based policies off-network.

questions.q: An engineer deploys Cisco Umbrella SIG for a remote branch. They want web traffic to be inspected by the cloud firewall and forwarded securely from the branch router. Which tunnel type should be configured on the ISR?
choices: L2TPv3 pseudowire
GETVPN group member tunnel
DMVPN Phase 3 spoke tunnel toward a hub ASA
IPsec IKEv2 tunnel to the
questions.explanation: Umbrella SIG supports IPsec IKEv2 tunnels from network devices (ISR, Meraki, etc.) to its cloud headends. Traffic is then inspected by Cloud-Delivered Firewall and secure web gateway. DMVPN, GETVPN, and L2TPv3 are not Umbrella SIG ingress methods.

questions.q: A Cisco Umbrella Investigate analyst notices a domain with a high risk score, recent registration, and fast-flux DNS. Which characteristic is the strongest indicator that this domain is likely used for malware C2?
choices: The domain uses Let's Encrypt certificates
Short TTL DNS records with rapidly rotating IPs
The domain is registered with a privacy proxy
The domain has HTTPS enabled with TLS 1.3
questions.explanation: Fast-flux DNS (very short TTL, IPs changing quickly across many ASNs) combined with a brand-new registration is a strong malware/botnet C2 signal. Let's Encrypt and WHOIS privacy are common on benign sites and are weak indicators on their own.

questions.q: An engineer designs a Secure Internet access for branch offices. Umbrella SIG policy must apply per user identity. Which integration makes Umbrella cloud firewall and SWG aware of user identities from Active Directory?
choices: Umbrella Roaming Client only
SNMP polling of the domain controller
Umbrella Virtual Appliance only
Umbrella Active Directory Connector
questions.explanation: Umbrella AD Connector pushes user-to-IP mappings from domain controllers so that Umbrella policies in-network can be user-scoped; for roaming users, the AnyConnect Umbrella/SWG module signs requests with identity. Neither RC nor VA alone provides AD user identity.

nodes.title: Mixed exam topics: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Some exam objectives don't fit neatly into a single domain — they span protocols, tools, or concepts covered briefly in multiple sections. These cards treat each item as a stand-alone fact, the way an exam question presents it: one concept, one answer.

flashcards.front: What is the difference between a hub, a switch, and a router?
flashcards.back: Hub: Layer 1, repeats every frame to all ports — all devices share bandwidth, collisions guaranteed. Switch: Layer 2, forwards frames using a MAC address table to only the destination port — full duplex, no collisions, each port gets full bandwidth. Router: Layer 3, makes forwarding decisions based on IP address, connects different networks. Hub is legacy; switches dominate LAN; routers are at network edges.

flashcards.front: What is RAID 5 and how many drives can it tolerate losing?
flashcards.back: RAID 5 stripes data and parity across at least 3 drives. Any single drive failure can be recovered by reconstructing missing data from the remaining drives and parity. It cannot tolerate 2 simultaneous drive failures. Effective capacity = (N-1) × drive size. Read performance is excellent; write requires parity recalculation. RAID 6 tolerates 2 failures using double parity.

flashcards.front: What does a proxy server do, and how does a forward proxy differ from a reverse proxy?
flashcards.back: Forward proxy: sits between clients and the internet on behalf of clients — used for content filtering, caching, and anonymizing outbound requests (the server sees the proxy's IP). Reverse proxy: sits in front of servers on behalf of the server — used for load balancing, SSL termination, caching, and hiding backend topology (the client sees the proxy's IP). Both intermediate HTTP, but they protect opposite sides.

flashcards.front: What is the purpose of a DMZ in network architecture?
flashcards.back: A demilitarized zone is a network segment between the untrusted internet and the trusted internal network, typically protected by two firewalls (or two interfaces on one firewall). Public-facing services (web, email, DNS) sit in the DMZ: internet can reach them but not the internal network; if the DMZ host is compromised, the inner firewall still blocks access to the internal LAN.

questions.q: A company wants to enforce user-based segmentation without rewriting ACLs on every switch. Users are tagged at ingress based on their ISE authorization policy, and enforcement decisions are made at egress switches using those tags. Which technology provides this model?
choices: Cisco TrustSec with Security Group Tags (SGT) and SGACLs
Private VLANs combined with port-based ACLs
MACsec with downlink encryption and ISE authorization
VRF-Lite with per-user route-leaking policies
questions.explanation: TrustSec assigns an SGT to each authenticated session at ingress via ISE authorization. The tag is propagated inline or via SXP, and egress devices apply SGACLs (source-SGT to destination-SGT matrices). This decouples policy from IP addresses and VLANs. MACsec provides link encryption, not segmentation.

questions.q: A security engineer is designing SXP (SGT Exchange Protocol) between ISE and an older Catalyst switch that does not support inline SGT tagging. Which statement about SXP is correct?
choices: SXP carries IP-to-SGT bindings over TCP.
SXP is a multicast protocol that floods SGT bindings to all devices
SXP uses UDP 4500 and requires IPsec for confidentiality
SXP can only run between ISE and Cisco ISR, not Catalyst switches
questions.explanation: SXP is a TCP-based protocol (default port 64999) that propagates IP-to-SGT bindings from tagging-capable devices (or ISE) to devices that cannot propagate tags inline. Speakers send bindings; Listeners receive and program their enforcement tables. allowing devices without inline tagging support to learn tags for enforcement

questions.q: A manufacturing company uses Cisco Stealthwatch (Secure Network Analytics) to detect anomalous behavior. Analysts want to identify lateral movement where an internal host suddenly starts communicating with many internal hosts on uncommon ports. Which Stealthwatch feature best detects this?
choices: Custom Security Events matching specific SGT flows
Behavioral algorithms on the High Concern Index with
Encrypted Traffic Analytics (ETA) for TLS visibility
Host Lock violations configured per host group
questions.explanation: Stealthwatch baselines normal east-west traffic patterns per host and raises the Concern Index when behavior deviates significantly, such as scanning many internal peers. ETA is for malware-in-encrypted-traffic, not lateral movement patterns, and Host Lock is a static policy violation mechanism.

questions.q: Security Operations wants to detect malware in encrypted TLS traffic without decrypting it. Which Cisco capability uses metadata such as initial data packet, sequence of packet lengths and times, and byte distribution to make this judgment?
choices: Encrypted Traffic Analytics (ETA)
Umbrella DNS-layer blocking
Cisco Tetration process hash matching
Snort3 with rule suppression
questions.explanation: ETA exports enhanced NetFlow with IDP (initial data packet), SPLT (sequence of packet lengths and times), and byte distribution. Stealthwatch + Cognitive Analytics + Talos build ML models that detect known malware families without breaking encryption.

questions.q: A company's Cisco Secure Email (ESA) is receiving a spike in spoofed messages claiming to be from the CEO. The domain has SPF published but many messages still reach the inbox. What additional email authentication mechanism should be deployed and enforced?
choices: Enable Sender IP Reputation (SBRS) to block low-reputation senders
Enable Graymail detection and safe unsubscribe
Use Forged Email Detection with a custom dictionary only
Configure DMARC with a reject policy in DNS.
questions.explanation: SPF alone only validates the envelope return-path; attackers can still spoof the From header. DMARC aligns SPF or DKIM with the From header and instructs receivers to reject non-aligned mail when p=reject is published. The ESA must also be configured to verify DMARC for inbound mail. combined with DKIM signing, and enable DMARC verification on the ESA

questions.q: A Cisco ESA administrator needs to prevent users from seeing marketing or promotional mail in their inboxes while still letting them opt out. Which ESA capability provides this?
choices: Forged Email Detection (FED)
Outbreak Filters with modify action
Graymail detection and Safe Unsubscribe
Content Filter with quarantine action for all .html mail
questions.explanation: Graymail detection classifies legitimate bulk mail (marketing, social, bulk) and can move it out of the inbox. Safe Unsubscribe lets users opt out via a proxy that protects them from malicious unsubscribe links. FED detects CEO impersonation, not graymail.

questions.q: A SOC analyst investigates a malware detection on an endpoint reported by Cisco Secure Endpoint. They need to see every file the process executed and every network connection it made, across time. Which Secure Endpoint feature provides this timeline?
choices: Prevalence widget on the SecureX ribbon
Indications of Compromise (IoC) dashboard
Retrospective Detection alerts
Device Trajectory (combined with File
questions.explanation: Device Trajectory shows a chronological process/file/network activity timeline for a specific host, while File Trajectory tracks where a specific SHA-256 was seen across the estate. Both together are essential for investigating scope and root cause. Retrospection re-evaluates past convictions when disposition changes.

questions.q: An analyst investigates suspicious PowerShell activity on a Windows endpoint using Cisco Secure Endpoint. They want to isolate the host from the network but keep communication with Secure Endpoint cloud for investigation. Which feature provides this?
choices: Host Isolation (Endpoint
Endpoint IoC retroactive scan
Simple Custom Detection list
Exclusion set bypass
questions.explanation: Secure Endpoint's Host Isolation quarantines an endpoint by blocking all network traffic except the connector's communication back to the cloud, allowing forensics without leaking lateral movement. It can be released remotely once the threat is contained.
